subject: Fix murmur32 on large strings (#1748)
reason: The change fixes a 32-bit int overflow in murmur32 (deps/lua/src/lstring.c), the hash used only by Lua's internal string-interning table (luaS_newlstr is its sole caller). The overflow only triggers for strings larger than ~8.59 GB, and even then it merely yields a wrong hash with no out-of-bounds access or crash. The hash is never exposed through any command reply; string-interning correctness is guaranteed by the memcmp fallback, so EVAL/FUNCTION results, data, persistence and replication are byte-identical on both builds. The only effect is Lua string-table bucket distribution (performance)
